text:
Irene: Heads-up — I want to run a coordinated validation sweep for the driver/kernel/firmware combo we've been testing. Target stack: kernel=5.15.120, nvidia-driver=535.54, fw=94.0. We saw a ~30% drop in Xid-79 in lab but need fleet-level validation before rolling to dedicated. Planning: staged canaries + 48h soak + workload replay + nightly telemetry diffs. Volunteers?
Alex: can you share the exact pass/fail criteria? also which regions/racks to target first (multi-az?)
Irene: pass criteria proposal: 
- no increase in Xid-rate vs baseline (30d median) more than +10%
- ECC corrected errors not rising >5 per GPU/day
- no new kernel oopses in kernel logs from compute hosts
- TPU/other infra unaffected (sanity checks)
Start in eu-west-1 on two racks (r12/r14) that host a mix of hosted and dedicated. If stable, expand to us-central canary.
Sam: PromQL snippets for monitoring: 
- Xid rate: sum(rate(gpu_xid_events_total[1h])) by (gpu_model)
- ECC corrected: sum(rate(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[1h])) by (gpu_id)
- kernel oops: increase in node_logs{severity=\"error\",component=\"kernel\"} with message =~ \"oops|BUG|GPU fault\"
I'll add these to the canary dash.
Maya: Proposed canary schedule: 
- Day 0: 2 hosts per rack (non-bursting jobs), run smoke tests (container start, /api inference baseline).
- Day 1-2: 48h soak with replay of production traces at 10-20% qps using replay-harness.
- Nightly: run 4h stress window (long sequences + concurrent batch jobs)
- Day 3: if green, expand to 10% capacity for 24h, then 50% for 6h, then full.
Chris: we need a specific rollback automation hook — if Xid rate crosses +20% of baseline or any new kernel oops seen, auto-drain and roll driver back. Also ensure dedicated customer hosts have immediate rollback (no staged expand).
Irene: agreed on rollback thresholds. I'll create a deploy pipeline that can auto-evict hosts when alert fires. deploy-bot, can you schedule the canary job tomorrow @ 03:00 UTC for eu-west-1 r12/r14?
deploy-bot: Canary job created: canary/gpu-stack/1798501234 — scheduled 2026-04-02T03:00:00Z. Notifying oncall.
Sam: small repro log we saw in lab (Xid 79):
```
Apr 01 12:34:11 gpu-node-314 kernel: NVRM: Xid (79): GPU has fallen off the bus.
Apr 01 12:34:11 gpu-node-314 kernel: nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
Apr 01 12:34:12 gpu-node-314 systemd: Container redis-worker exited code=134
```
We need to ensure the new driver doesn't change bus rescan timing that caused the os-level OOMs in one previous case.
Alex: For the telemetry diffs, let's compute daily percent change and surface p50/p95 latency impact too. If generation latency p95 increases >5% for hosted API, block. Also capture token-level tail latency samples.
Maya: I'll own the replay harness and soak config. I'll seed traces with both short and long sequences; long sequences tend to hit KV cache paths which historically triggered GPU memory fragmentation.
Chris: small ops note — when draining a node we must set scheduler weight=0 then politely cordon for 10m, then drain pods with graceful timeout 120s, then force if still stuck. This reduced failed evictions during the last FW rollback.
Irene: adding a preflight smoke checklist: 
- kernel-headers present on node, module build ok
- nvidia-smi returns all GPUs present
- run quick workload: docker run --rm myorg/gpu-smoke:latest ./smoke.sh (3 iterations)
- check kernel log for fresh oops for 15m
I'll paste the exact commands in the playbook shortly.
Alex: QA/alerting notes: add a short-lived metric 'canary_xid_ratio' = xid_rate(canary)/xid_rate(baseline) and set composite alert when >1.2 for 30m. Also add alert silence rules so we don't spam on transient spikes.
Irene: good. also adding a metric for ECC corrected errors per gpu per 24h, alert if >10.
Maya: timeline OK for me. I'll run a dry-run tonight in staging with the same stack and post results.
qa-bot: Staging dry-run completed: kernel=5.15.120 driver=535.54 fw=94.0 — smoke.sh passed (3/3), no oops in 1h. See logs: http://internal/logs/1798501234/staging-dryrun
Chris: remember to include a mix of preemptible instances and dedicated-guests in the soak; hardware variance hits different failure modes.
Sam: one more check — ensure mig/cuda compute instances run the same driver; we had a mismatch before where cuda-toolkit picked up older libnvidia. Add docker image with pinned libnvidia as part of smoke.
Irene: Nice catch. I'll pin images.
Alex: I'll update dashboards and alerting, and will monitor the first 6h post-canary closely.
Irene: OK team — action items: Maya run staging dry-run (in progress), Sam will instrument PromQL + dash, Alex will patch alerts, Chris will prepare rollback playbook, I'll wire the deploy pipeline. We'll reconvene 4h after the canary starts. Please ack when you see this. :thumbsup:
Maya: ack :thumbsup:
Sam: ack
Chris: ack
Alex: ack
Irene: Thanks — leaving notes in runbook and will tag oncall during rollout.
